thread.title: Tech Today: Tesla's Bizarre Q&A, Xiaomi IPO, Defending Spotify

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Tesla's Bizarre Q&A, Xiaomi IPO, Defending Spotify
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Tesla's truly bizarre, odd, unorthodox call Getty Images Tesla ( TSLA ) shares this morning are down $17.76, or 6%, at $283.39, after CEO Elon Musk at one point abruptly cut off the analysts on last night's Q&A following the company's Q1 report .
The analysts are calling the discussion "bizarre."
One of the analysts Musk abruptly dismissed, Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein , today reiterates his Market Perform rating, writing that the call was "a unique experience, to say the least."
Beyond the "theatrics," writes Sacconaghi, "most importantly to the investment thesis, Tesla appeared to push out its Model 3 gross margin target of 25% by 6-9 months." He thinks the company's statement yesterday that it will be profitable by next quarter is "a somewhat unlikely scenario."
Jim Cramer on CNBC this morning speculates this is Musk's last call-that he'll just do away with doing calls. "He has declared he doesn't want to talk to the analysts," said Cramer. Cramer also suggested if Tesla wants to ultimately raise capital-something most on the Street believe it will have to do-Musk could step down from the CEO role.
CNBC's David Faber made a comparison between Musk and Enron 's one-time CEO, Jeff Skilling , who was known for labeling people who asked questions with derogatory names.
Legendary Keller's next thing One interesting side takeaway from the Tesla call: Musk was asked about legendary chip designer Jim Keller , who, it was announced last week , has left his job at Tesla's self-driving group to take a job at Intel ( INTC ).
Musk, calling Keller "a great guy," noted Keller's dream was to "kind of redesign how server architecture works.
"It's not something that I find a lot interesting," said Musk, "but it's something that Jim-it's been a sort of a personal dream for Jim to do, and that's why he went to Intel."
Xiaomi preps Hong Kong IPO Xiaomi , the privately held Chinese smartphone maker, late yesterday filed to go public on the Hong Kong stock exchange to raise $10 billion, with underwriting from CLSA , Goldman Sachs , and Morgan Stanley .
Founder and Chairman Lei Jun writes that Xiaomi intends to "cap" its profit in smartphones at 5% , adding that "delivering sustained, high-quality user experience is more important than pursuing one-time hardware profits." Jun pledges to return any excess profit in smartphones to the company's users.
Xiaomi bills itself as "an Internet company with smartphones and smart hardware connected by an IoT platform at its core."
The company made almost 115 billion Chinese renminbi in revenue last year, equivalent to U.S. $18 billion . The company had a gross profit of $2.5 billion and an operating profit of $1.9 billion.
The filing lists a net negative income of almost $7 billion, but the company explained through a spokesperson that the net loss is "not an operating loss," but rather the result of an accounting revision of the company's convertible redeemed preference shares last year, a one-time item.
Spotify sinks Shares of Spotify Technology ( SPOT ), the streaming music pioneer that went public April 3 , are down $16, or 9.4%, at $154, after it reported paid subscribers of 75 million at quarter's end, slightly below consensus, and forecast revenue this quarter lower than the Street has been modeling.
Among bulls defending the stock is Canaccord Genuity 's Maria Ripps , who reiterates a Buy rating, writing that this first report was "tightly in sync" with what the company said during its roadshow .
She thinks the company "delivered" in terms of audience growth, noting that "having launched in Israel, Romania, South Africa, and Vietnam during Q1 (bringing total markets served to 65, compared with NFLX at ~130), SPOT plans on entering more markets in 2018 and appears poised to continue steady expansion for the foreseeable future."
We're waiting to hear from the bears, though there aren't that many.
Defending Square Another loser from last night, payments pioneer Square ( SQ ), is actually recovering from the worst of its after-hours loses, after its Q1 revenue beat expectations but its profit came in merely in line with consensus, and it offered a forecast for profit that missed. The stock is down 41 cents, or 0.8%, at $48.25.
The stock has gotten one upgrade this morning, from Stifel Nicolaus 's Scott Devitt , who raised the shares to Buy from Hold and raised his price target to $55 from $46, writing that the report was "impressive" and that he supports the company's desire to spend more to grow its business.
Square's Ebitda target for this year is the same as it was, even though the company raised its revenue outlook.
"We strongly support Square's decision to reinvest in key strategic areas," writes Devitt, "as we believe this will ultimately support higher levels of growth over the long term and effectively widen its competitive position."
Another loser from last night losing more ground this morning is Fitbit ( FIT ), down 49 cents, or almost 9%, at $5.01, after it reported blowout early orders for its smartwatch, the " Versa ," but sales of traditional fitness trackers will weigh on this quarter's revenue.
Qorvo Slumps, Logitech Surges One winner from last night is struggling this morning: Qorvo (QRVO), the wireless chip maker that counts Apple (AAPL) as a big customer. Its report yesterday afternoon beat expectations, but the outlook for this quarter fell short. Its shares are down $2.85, or almost 4%, at $71.39, reversing a small after-hours gain last night.
Harsh Kumar at Piper Jaffray this morning reiterates an Overweight rating, and a $90 price target, writing that he is "overall very pleased" with the report.
Mobile is not as bad as feared for Qorvo, thanks to more demand from Chinese smartphone makers than expected. He thinks the two most important things in the report were that "they have won the superpad and thus the ramp in BAW later this year," an allusion to getting more share at Apple in the next iPhone; and that some weakness in Qorvo's gross margin -a "soft patch," he calls it-"is completely temporary" and should be alleviated in the company's September quarter.
A winner from yesterday that's surging today is Logitech (LOGI), the maker of connected devices and peripherals. Its fiscal Q4 revenue of $592 million and EPS of 32 cents easily topped expectations for $555.6 million and 23 cents. The company reiterated its forecast for revenue growth this year to rise "in the high single digits."
Logitech is up $3.47, or 9.4%, at $40.21. I'll have more later today with the company's CEO Bracken Darrell .
